verdicts.text: Error handling in Go's `apply` may also be achieved using an `error` channel.
verdicts.evidence: The Go SDK's ApplyT takes a callback of the form `func(T) (U, error)`, and errors reject the output. The SDK helpers are all written this way, e.g. `o.ApplyTWithContext(ctx, func(_ context.Context, v any) (string, error) {...})`. I found no error-channel mechanism in pulumi/pulumi's sdk/go/pulumi/types.go. The docs' own "Handling errors in apply" section describes only the `(U, error)` return and `ApplyTWithContext`.
verdicts.intuition_flag: Go's `error` channel is not a Pulumi ApplyT mechanism; the sentence looks like a plausible-sounding hallucination.

verdicts.text: Secret values are decrypted and made available in plain text to the program at runtime, and can be read using any of the standard `pulumi.Config` getters, though using the non-secret getters for a secret is not recommended since it does not mark transitive uses as secret.
verdicts.evidence: In pulumi/pulumi sdk/nodejs/config.ts, `get` returns the raw decrypted string from `getConfig`, while `getSecret` wraps it via `makeSecret(v)`. The plain getter therefore works on secret values but does not mark the result as secret, so downstream uses are not tracked as secret. A commented-out warning ("value is a secret; use getSecret instead of get") shows the SDK team also recommends the secret variants.

verdicts.evidence: Auto-generated CLI reference: "Publish a package to the Private Registry... The package can be a provider or a schema... When <provider> is specified as a local path, Pulumi executes the provider binary to extract its package schema." So `pulumi package publish` supports executable/binary providers. The Pulumi Cloud requirement is implied by the Private Registry, but I did not find it stated in a source (the GitHub search was rate-limited).
verdicts.framing_note: The source says publish accepts provider binaries and plugins and targets the Private Registry. The claim's "Pulumi Cloud customers" scoping is implied rather than stated.
